classification.difficultyReason: Translate distance from 6 into a two-sided strict interval, filter for even whole numbers and plot the survivors; also recognise an empty set after combining interval and parity restrictions.

content.prompt: Represent each set on a number line.

answer.worked: Mark 1, 2 and 5 with filled dots on a whole-number line.
Mark 0, 1, 5 and 6 with filled dots on a whole-number line.
Mark 2 and 3 with filled dots on a whole-number line.
Mark only 4 with a filled dot on a whole-number line.
The whole numbers less than 5 are $\{0,1,2,3,4\}$. Mark each with a filled dot.

children.label: f
children.prompt: $\{\text{even whole numbers less than 5 units from }6\}$

answer.worked: Less than 5 units from 6 means greater than 1 and less than 11. The even whole numbers in this interval are $\{2,4,6,8,10\}$. Mark each with a filled dot.
The odd whole numbers between 0 and 8 are $\{1,3,5,7\}$. Mark each with a filled dot.

children.label: h
children.prompt: the set of prime numbers less than 12

answer.worked: The numbers less than 12 with exactly two positive factors are $2,3,5,7,11$. Mark each with a filled dot; 1 is not prime.

children.label: i
children.prompt: the set of numbers that are 2 units from 3

answer.worked: Two units to the left of 3 is $3-2=1$; two units to the right is $3+2=5$. Mark 1 and 5 with filled dots.
The even whole numbers between 3 and 9 are $\{4,6,8\}$. Mark each with a filled dot.
Inclusive includes both endpoints, so the set is $\{1,2,3,4\}$. Mark each with a filled dot.
The only whole number between $3\frac12$ and $4\frac12$ is 4, which is even. The set is empty, so no points are marked.

spec.description: An unmarked number line represents the empty set; teacher evidence supplies the empty-set symbol.
spec.mathematics: No odd whole number lies strictly between 3.5 and 4.5.
